Definition: of Hebrew origin (H6439); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite:--Phanuel.
BiblicalUsage: Phanuel is the father of Anna the prophetess, who served God in the temple with fastings and prayers night and day. When the child Jesus is brought to the temple, Anna, the daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher, is there to give thanks and speak of Him to all who look for redemption.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Phanuel's name is remembered because of his daughter: he raised a prophetess who waited in the temple, and she was there on the day the redemption she waited for arrived.
